2024 has been a big year for enthusiasts, as many of the world's most renowned supercar and hypercar makers have released new, breathtaking models. For some, like Bentley and Aston Martin, these are extravagant low-volume cars that build on previous high-quality engineering, but others, like McLaren and Ferrari, announced new halo models that are set to redefine performance for the modern age.

As one would expect, vehicles such as this don't come cheap. These are the best models from the most coveted automakers on the planet and, as such, they cost more money than most can even imagine. While there's been no shortage of reveals this year, we wanted to take a look at the 10 most expensive vehicles revealed this year. All of them cost upwards of $2 million, but the most expensive vehicle on the list claims the crown by a mile.
We aimed to only include vehicles on this list with a production run, no one-offs (except for one notable exception), and only one model per manufacturer. They've been ordered from least to most expensive, and we've only included models with confirmed or approximate pricing.

It's been a long time since production of the P1 ended, and McLaren has finally remedied this halo-car dry spell with its successor: the W1. The name comes from the brand's "World Championship" mindset and is a tribute to the company's first Driver's and Constructor's World Championships in 1974, the latter of which the brand nabbed once again in 2024.

Obviously, there's a lot of weight to this name, but the car lives up to it thanks to [some truly impressive performance specs](https://carbuzz.com/reveal-mclaren-w1-hypercar/). A twin-turbo V8 hybrid powertrain boasts over 1,200 horsepower, making it the most powerful road-legal McLaren ever made. It combines that performance with a McLaren Aerocell monocoque and F1-derived suspension, allowing for a dry weight of a mere 3,084 lbs. The top speed is 217, and the car looks like a gorgeous evolution of the brand's famous design language. It's everything we wanted out of the next-gen McLaren hypercar,

In a long-awaited return of the legendary design house, Bertone has unveiled the GB100: a wedge masterpiece that will become [the design house's first hypercar](https://carbuzz.com/bertone-gb110-makes-official-debut-1100-hp-twin-turbocharged-v10/). Powered by a twin-turbo 5.2-liter V10 engine, it will produce over 1,100 horsepower and rocket to 217 mph, according to the design studio. The company isn't worried about 0-60 mph times, instead going much bigger, and saying it'll shoot from 0-186 mph in just 12.9 seconds.
The design is incredible, a mix [between the 1950s and the 1970s](https://carbuzz.com/bertone-perfect-modern-jaguar-decade-ago/), and pays homage to recent supercars from Lamborghini and McLaren. The company even says it will be the first hypercar to run off fuel made of plastic waste, but we'll have to see if that happens when the first of the 33-car production run makes it into customer's hands.

Aston Martin has been enjoying releasing highly limited runs of supercars over the last few years, all building off of one another. The newest entrant to this list is the [Valiant](https://carbuzz.com/cars/aston-martin/valiant/), which is an evolution of the [Valour](https://carbuzz.com/cars/aston-martin/valour/) based on a bespoke commission created by F1 World Champion Fernando Alonso. It looks properly mean, with an exaggerated body kit and massive wing that make it look ready for takeoff.
Of course, another iteration of the brand's incredible V12 is under the hood, and here it's mated to a six-speed manual transmission with some of the most beautiful exposed linkages. The brand hasn't announced any performance numbers, so we have no idea how quickly it will rocket around a racetrack, but it will likely only see use in such a fashion very rarely, [given that only 38 will be produced](https://carbuzz.com/aston-martin-valiant-keeps-the-manual-v12-sports-car-dream-alive/) for the exorbitant price of $2.5 million.

Look, we know we said no one-offs, but how can you not include a $31 million vehicle? Before Rolls-Royce embarked on the Droptail journey there wasn't anything even remotely this expensive for sale.
It's bathed in a "timeless white" color that is meant to look solid most of the time and complex under the lights thanks to aluminum and glass particles in the paint. 8,000 hours of woodwork make up the interior, and the clock face is the most complex ever fit to a Rolls-Royce. The watch face took two years alone to develop and five months to fit in place. Along with the innumerable other pieces of the car that were perfected and hand-placed, the unbelievable price tag is a little more understandable. A little.
